reason: The passage depicts a hierarchical structure rather than collaboration. God commands Abram unilaterally (וַיֹּאמֶר יְהוָה אֶל־אַבְרָם), Abram obeys without recorded discussion or negotiation (וַיֵּלֶךְ אַבְרָם כַּאֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר אֵלָיו יְהוָה), and others (Sarai, Lot, servants) follow Abram's leadership. While the household does travel together toward Canaan as a group, the text shows no evidence of genuine collaboration, shared decision-making, or joint leadership. The structure is one of command and obedience rather than collaborative partnership between leaders and people.
